3. Reference Calibration: No human-scored reference images were provided, so this criterion does not apply.

4. Leniency Bias: I did not rubber-stamp the Router. I independently verified the bird count (5 not 6) and confirmed the sparkle effect is intentional rather than noise. I also noted the bird leg fusion issue that the Router mentioned but may have underweighted.

5. Harshness Bias: I avoided over-penalizing. The sparkle texture anomaly (severity 2) was treated as an intentional stylistic choice per prompt, not a defect. Only the bird count error and minor leg fusion affected scores. One atom failure (count) reduced alignment from perfect but didn't tank the overall score since 9/10 atoms pass.

6. Atom Score Review: Each qa_score is justified by visual evidence and expert confirmation. tax_scores are all 1.0 as no taxonomy-specific failures were attributed to individual atoms (the cock vs quail issue is a global taxonomy mismatch, not an atom-level failure).

7. Upward Override Justification: No upward overrides were made. All positive verdicts were independently verified through visual inspection and expert evidence. The bird count failure was confirmed visually despite the detector finding 7 boxes (which I correctly interpreted as overlapping/false positives).

Final scores remain unchanged from initial assessment as they were already accurate and well-justified.
